The relation to Strategy's ON_LEAVE state remains unresolved, and local signing or legal-closure descriptions do not become universal completion rules."},"baseline_placement":{"canonical_id":null,"owner_key":"capability:episode--encounter-administration","parent_key":null,"tier":null},"baseline_unresolved":["ancestry","canonical_id","code_allocation","feature_association"],"baseline_version":"0.1","canonical_id":"CT1-BEC-CARE-ADMINISTRATION-INFORMATION-ENABLEMENT.CT2-BEC-EPISODE-ENCOUNTER-ADMINISTRATION.PR-ENCOUNTER-LIFECYCLE-PROCESS","canonical_name":"Encounter Lifecycle Process","category":null,"governed_definition_latex":"
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Episode \& Encounter Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the clinical and administrative lifecycle of an acute, emergency, inpatient, or outpatient encounter between a patient and healthcare services.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Planned /\allowbreak{} Booked → Arrived → Triaged /\allowbreak{} Ingested → Active In-Progress → Discharged → Completed /\allowbreak{} Encoded (Scoped illustration; ON\_LEAVE relationship unresolved)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Planned / Booked}}: Elective admission or clinic appointment scheduled.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Arrived}}: Patient presents at facility or emergency desk.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Triaged / Ingested}}: Clinical triage category assigned; encounter record activated.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Active In-Progress}}: Inpatient care, bedside monitoring, and clinical orders actively underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharged}}: Patient clinically discharged; care-place vacated.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Completed / Encoded}}: Clinical documentation finalized, ICD/\allowbreak{}DRG coding completed, and encounter legally closed.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: These completion criteria retain their locally described applicability; they do not establish universal signing, legal closure or originating authority over clinical information. Finalisation, signing and legal qualification remain distinct. The relationship with Strategy \texttt{\seqsplit{ON\_LEAVE}}, including applicability and transitions, remains unresolved.



\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

{"ancestry_status":"proposed","architectural_status":"Canonical","baseline_description":{"Process Overview":"Discharge progression coordinates the confirmations and practical requirements around leaving care. Clinical readiness, medications, destination arrangements and transport are related but distinct contributions, and the source progression retains its stated local applicability. Operational coordination does not originate the clinical discharge decision or prove that another provider assumed responsibility."},"baseline_placement":{"canonical_id":null,"owner_key":"capability:discharge-management","parent_key":null,"tier":null},"baseline_unresolved":["ancestry","canonical_id","code_allocation","feature_association"],"baseline_version":"0.1","canonical_id":"CT1-BEC-CARE-OPERATIONS-COORDINATION-ENABLEMENT.CT2-BEC-DISCHARGE-MANAGEMENT.PR-DISCHARGE-PROGRESSION-PROCESS","canonical_name":"Discharge Progression Process","category":null,"governed_definition_latex":"
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Management}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the multidisciplinary coordination of patient discharge planning, pharmacy reconciliation, transport, and community handover.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Discharge Planning Initiated → Clinical Readiness Confirmed → Medications Reconciled → Transport \& Services Booked → Discharge Summary Signed → Physically Departed (Illustrative preparation; publication, authorisation and exit distinct)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Planning Initiated}}: Estimated Date of Discharge (EDD) set on admission.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Readiness Confirmed}}: Attending medical team declares patient fit for discharge.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Medications Reconciled}}: Hospital pharmacy reconciles and dispenses discharge medications.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Transport \& Services Booked}}: Community nursing, home equipment, and patient transport booked.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Summary Signed}}: Applicable signed summary is available/\allowbreak{}published and may be communicated before departure where the Business behaviour requires it; signing, finalisation, publication and discharge authorisation remain distinct.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Physically Departed}}: Confirmed physical exit triggers departure notifications, updated bed-state communication and finalised-summary dispatch to external care providers under \texttt{\seqsplit{FEAT-HSO-29}}; care-place turnover follows its own responsibility.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Timing reconciliation}: Preparation, information availability/\allowbreak{}publication, applicable discharge authorisation and physical exit are distinct. Earlier preparation/\allowbreak{}communication is permitted; it does not realise a Feature triggered by confirmed exit. This illustrated local pathway establishes neither universal publication timing nor a universal discharge state machine, and adds no inferred publication event or authorisation state.



\item 
\textbf{Preserved uncertainty}: Summary signing and finalisation are not universal equivalents. Detailed applicability, discharge-authority workflows and timing beyond the established preparation/\allowbreak{}confirmed-exit distinction remain unestablished.



\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

Dispatch, recipient acceptance, result binding and requester closure remain distinct facts even where a source checkpoint combines them."},"baseline_placement":{"canonical_id":null,"owner_key":"capability:order-administration","parent_key":null,"tier":null},"baseline_unresolved":["ancestry","canonical_id","code_allocation","feature_association"],"baseline_version":"0.1","canonical_id":"CT1-BEC-CARE-ADMINISTRATION-INFORMATION-ENABLEMENT.CT2-BEC-ORDER-ADMINISTRATION.PR-CLOSED-LOOP-ORDER-PROGRESSION-PROCESS","canonical_name":"Closed-Loop Order Progression Process","category":null,"governed_definition_latex":"
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Order Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the rigorous, closed-loop tracking of diagnostic pathology, radiology, and procedural orders from requisition to result correlation, preventing dropped or unfulfilled investigations.



\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: These examples describe a diagnostic/\allowbreak{}procedural progression and do not exclude medication from the broader Order Administration responsibility. Specimen and result checkpoints are scoped. The signed requisition/\allowbreak{}report requirements remain within this illustrated scope; signing is not universally equivalent to finalisation or authority. Result consumption/\allowbreak{}binding does not define originating validity, authority, authorship or legal status.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Requisition Placed → Order Dispatched → Specimen Collected /\allowbreak{} Scheduled → In-Execution → Preliminary Result Bound → Final Result Bound → Closed /\allowbreak{} Verified (Scoped diagnostic/\allowbreak{}procedural illustration)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Requisition Placed}}: Electronic order created and signed by requesting clinician.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Order Dispatched}}: Order routed and accepted by performing diagnostic service. This local compound checkpoint retains routing and recipient acceptance as distinct facts; dispatch alone establishes neither receipt nor acceptance. Behaviour \texttt{\seqsplit{Received}} is not equated with this checkpoint without evidence.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Collected / Scheduled}}: Bio-specimen collected or imaging appointment booked.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Execution}}: Laboratory analysis or diagnostic scanning underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Preliminary Result Bound}}: Critical or interim observations published and linked to order.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Final Result Bound}}: Authoritative diagnostic report signed and bound to order.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Closed / Verified}}: Requesting clinician acknowledges result; order closed. This Order-closure checkpoint does not establish diagnostic-content verification, approval or clinical incorporation.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

Neither a transmitted referral nor the local compound acceptance/waitlist checkpoint establishes actual responsibility transfer."},"baseline_placement":{"canonical_id":null,"owner_key":"capability:referral-administration","parent_key":null,"tier":null},"baseline_unresolved":["ancestry","canonical_id","code_allocation","feature_association"],"baseline_version":"0.1","canonical_id":"CT1-BEC-CARE-ADMINISTRATION-INFORMATION-ENABLEMENT.CT2-BEC-REFERRAL-ADMINISTRATION.PR-REFERRAL-PROGRESSION-PROCESS","canonical_name":"Referral Progression Process","category":null,"governed_definition_latex":"
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Referral Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the end-to-end operational progression of an incoming clinical referral from receipt through specialist clinical triage, booking, and final service acceptance.



\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: This illustrates a specialist booking/\allowbreak{}attendance pathway; Referral does not universally require acceptance, scheduling, attendance or discharge, or establish delivery, responsibility actually assumed or Transfer of Care. Decline, rejection and redirection remain valid dispositions without invented transition paths. \texttt{\seqsplit{Accepted / Waitlisted}} is a local compound checkpoint, not universal equivalence between acceptance and waitlisting.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Submitted → Intake Validated → Clinically Triaged → Accepted /\allowbreak{} Waitlisted → Scheduled → Consultation Attended → Discharged /\allowbreak{} Rejected (Illustrative specialist pathway; dispositions vary)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Submitted}}: Electronic referral received from GP or external facility.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Intake Validated}}: Administrative validation of patient details, mandatory fields, and tests.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinically Triaged}}: Senior clinician assigns urgency category (e.g., Cat 1 urgent within 30 days).



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Accepted / Waitlisted}}: Referral accepted and placed onto the specialty waitlist.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Scheduled}}: Outpatient appointment allocated and patient notified.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Consultation Attended}}: Patient seen; initial specialist assessment completed.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharged / Rejected}}: Referral completed and discharged back to primary care, or formally rejected with clinical rationale.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

{"ancestry_status":"proposed","architectural_status":"Canonical","baseline_description":{"Process Overview":"This Process makes authorship and changing document standing intelligible through the locally described review, amendment and withdrawal circumstances. It preserves prior versions rather than treating correction as erasure. The illustration does not require every document to pass through every stage or make finalisation, signing, legal qualification and originating authority equivalent."},"baseline_placement":{"canonical_id":null,"owner_key":"capability:clinical-record-administration","parent_key":null,"tier":null},"baseline_unresolved":["ancestry","canonical_id","code_allocation","feature_association"],"baseline_version":"0.1","canonical_id":"CT1-BEC-CARE-ADMINISTRATION-INFORMATION-ENABLEMENT.CT2-BEC-CLINICAL-RECORD-ADMINISTRATION.PR-CLINICAL-DOCUMENT-LIFECYCLE-PROCESS","canonical_name":"Clinical Document Lifecycle Process","category":null,"governed_definition_latex":"
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Record Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the versioning, clinical sign-off, addenda, superseding, and legal status of clinical documents (discharge summaries, specialist letters, advance care directives).



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Draft → Preliminary → Final Signed → Amended /\allowbreak{} Addended → Superseded → Entered-in-Error (Scoped illustration; no universal document lifecycle)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Draft}}: Incomplete clinical document saved during consultation.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Preliminary}}: Document authored pending senior registrar or consultant countersignature.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Final Signed}}: Authoritative clinical document legally signed and published.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Amended / Addended}}: Governed supplementary clinical addendum appended to signed document.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Superseded}}: Entire document replaced by a newer revision; prior version retained for audit.

% !TeX root = ../Harmonia-EA-Capability-Map.tex

\chapter{Reading the proposed architecture}\label{model:guide}\label{guide}
Version 0.2-draft incorporates the human-reviewed BEC candidate hierarchy and a bounded reconciliation of compatible Stage-2 material. It does not replace the governed Markdown RAD or declare an architecture domain complete. The 0.1 publication remains independently reproducible. Its identities, definitions, semantic boundaries, source traceability and established relationships are preserved, with genuine conflicts explicitly retained outside the current BEC hierarchy.

Element, naming, direct-placement, complete-path and relationship status are separate assertions. A Canonical responsibility can have a Proposed CT3 placement and Proposed structural identifier. A Candidate concern remains Candidate even when a best placement is proposed. Source uncertainty is retained in the governed appendix; the proposal makes a current judgement rather than leaving the concept floating.

Capability, Feature, Function, Service and Process remain different constructs. Every current Feature has a meaningful BEC CT3 frame. Features whose original semantics have no adjudicated frame are preserved in the explicit unresolved register. Directly Capability-owned behaviour remains valid. Services expose a client contract; Processes chain Functions where meaningful. None of those semantics requires a Feature-to-Function-to-Service-to-Process containment chain.

The fourteen Canonical EC responsibilities become CT2s under three Proposed CT1 frames. The application of the structural ID grammar to ECs is itself Proposed; EC-01 through EC-14 remain stable Reference IDs and historical structural aliases. Reuse does not mandate centralised services, separate processes or distributed responsibility.

Downstream Application Component derivation may use this current proposed model as its working assumption, while retaining every assertion status. Derive cohesive responsibility centres from capabilities; do not force them to reproduce current Mneme, Mnemosyne, Ponos, Calliope or other component boundaries. No capability in this publication allocates an application component, module, process or deployment.

AX-01/04 preserve healthcare meaning over machinery; AX-05 separates active use from durable establishment; AX-06 qualifies source authority; AX-07/08/09 distinguish governed action, meaningful evidence and diagnostics; AX-10/11/12 preserve operational integrity; AX-13 governs boundary publication; AX-14/15/17 preserve distinctions, uncertainty and authority; AX-16/18 preserve entity progression without inferred domain authority. CM-R01 through CM-R05 are reviewed through complete placement, bounded responsibility, explicit definitions, cohesive roots and unique current display names.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

This reusable capability keeps managed healthcare entities identifiable and their relationships structurally intelligible. It supplies common identity, alias and relationship behaviour recurring in persons, practitioners, organisations, locations and devices. Reuse concerns those architectural responsibilities, allowing the healthcare-specific meaning of each entity to remain with its governing context.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Identify, classify, relate, and maintain the structural integrity of managed healthcare and administrative entities throughout the enterprise landscape.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Uniquely identifying core domain entities (Persons, Practitioners, Roles, Organisations, Locations, Services, Devices).



\item
Resolving and maintaining multi-authority identifier systems and aliases without destructive overwriting.



\item
Representing and traversing multi-dimensional relationships (affiliations, organizational hierarchies, physical location trees, care team memberships).



\item
Maintaining referential integrity across interconnected entity graphs.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not own physical database relational tables or foreign key constraints (Domain 04/\allowbreak{}07).



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Relationship integrity is not a physical database design. Correlating entities does not establish originating clinical identity authority or a new standalone Correlation capability.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Governed Information Operations; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Context Management preserves the circumstances in which information and activity have meaning as they cross processing boundaries. Subject, encounter, provider, service and security context must remain attributable and consistent rather than be reconstructed from convenient local assumptions. Its reuse is especially significant in multi-hop activity where a syntactically valid message can otherwise lose the context required for legitimate interpretation.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Establish, validate, propagate, and preserve the execution, clinical, security, and administrative context within which information and activities have meaning.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Binding the subject of care, encounter, ordering provider, and healthcare service context to in-flight messages and transactions.



\item
Propagating tamper-evident, attributable security context across asynchronous, multi-hop operational boundaries.



\item
Ensuring context preservation during cross-protocol transformations across disparate healthcare exchange formats and protocols.



\item
Detecting and rejecting requests where mandatory operational or clinical context is missing or inconsistent.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Bounded reusable context responsibility may be realised through participation across gateways, activity execution and information-access boundaries. Participation does not transfer semantic ownership.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Context participation does not transfer semantic ownership. Generic context management and assurance-specific context semantics contribute together without allocating a new central Context Service.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Governed Information Operations; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Managed State \& Lifecycle provides reusable responsibility for valid progression, temporal applicability and non-destructive change. A directory relationship, clinical document and operational work item have different business states, yet all need an intelligible distinction between current standing, historical state and invalid transitions. The capability captures that recurrence without replacing each subject's lifecycle meaning.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Govern the current and historical state, effective temporal periods, state transition validations, and lifecycle progression of managed integration artifacts and entities.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Defining and enforcing valid state transition state machines (e.g., \texttt{\seqsplit{REQUESTED}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{VALIDATED}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{IN\_PROGRESS}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{COMPLETED}}).



\item
Maintaining temporal validity intervals (effective start and end dates) for relationships, credentials, and states.



\item
Supporting non-destructive state progression, preserving historical state versions for longitudinal review.



\item
Rejecting illegal or out-of-order state transitions while accommodating idempotent replay.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not define thread-level mutexes or database transaction isolation levels.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Business lifecycle integrity does not prescribe locks, database isolation or worker implementation, and illustrative state names do not define every subject's transitions.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Governed Information Operations; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Information Management provides the recurring ability to represent and maintain governed information through validation, preservation, retrieval and versioned change. It accommodates both responsive active use and authoritative durable preservation while keeping those responsibilities separate. This distinction allows availability and working state to support care without turning a cache into durable truth.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Validate, represent, persist, retrieve, version, and manage governed clinical, administrative, and operational information assets.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Validating inbound information structures against canonical information constraints.



\item
Providing authoritative durable persistence for historical health records and administrative registries.



\item
Managing active distributed working memory representations for low-latency retrieval.



\item
Governing document versioning, supersession, amendments, and retractions without data loss.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Architectural Principle}: Enforces the foundational separation between \emph{active distributed state access} and \emph{authoritative durable state preservation} (Axiom AX-05).



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Engine capabilities provide machinery under Harmonia semantics. Persistence success does not establish information authority or make the platform the originator of the represented facts.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Governed Information Operations; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

Standards govern the external representation while internal management semantics remain private.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Providing multi-protocol boundary adaptation for healthcare standards (HL7 v2, FHIR REST, DICOM, secure messaging).



\item
Executing bidirectional structural and semantic transformations between legacy formats and canonical representations.



\item
Ensuring reliable addressed delivery and fan-out distribution to external clinical endpoints.



\item
Processing and distinguishing technical delivery acknowledgements from business acknowledgements.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Boundary Rule}: Egress terminates Harmonia management of the emitted representation (Axiom AX-13).



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Egress ends Harmonia management of the emitted representation. Retained delivery evidence does not extend control over an external recipient or transfer payload authority.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Event \& Subscription connects significant changes with participants whose registered interests match them. It makes event ingestion, correlation, interest criteria and notification reusable across clinical and operational contexts. The architectural meaning is the relationship between a change and an interested consumer, rather than the broker constructs used to carry it.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Publish, ingest, correlate, filter, and syndicate events and subscription-driven changes across the enterprise landscape.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Ingesting operational and clinical event triggers from external systems and internal state changes.



\item
Managing topic- and criteria-based event subscriptions for internal and external consumers.



\item
Evaluating dynamic subscription filters to match event payloads with interested subscriber criteria.



\item
Delivering asynchronous event notifications reliably to registered subscribers.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Decoupling Note}: Defined strictly in terms of event publishing, criteria matching, and notification delivery; entirely independent of broker topics, partitions, or queues.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Receiving a notification does not determine the consumer's business response; topics and queues do not define the capability.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Define, instantiate, match, assign, dispatch, supervise, and progress coordinated operational and clinical activity units.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Instantiating operational work items (Work Orders, To Dos, synthetic platform Tasks) in response to triggers.



\item
Matching and assigning work units to eligible human or automated performers and roles based on policy rules.



\item
Dispatching work units to their assigned performers with acknowledgement according to the applicable interaction contract.



\item
Supervising execution progress, tracking timeouts, managing escalations, and handling activity interruptions.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Decoupling Note}: Free of worker threads, thread pools, execution daemons, or specific workflow runtime engines.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Coordination does not confer clinical work allocation or judgement. The capability specifies neither worker threads nor a particular execution engine.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Coordinated Activity \& Interaction; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Provenance \& Traceability preserves the meaningful attribution and history needed to explain information and significant activity. It connects source, transformation and required checkpoints without making every internal mechanism permanent evidence. Its recurring contribution supports accountability, reconstruction and assurance use while retaining the context that makes a recorded fact evidentially relevant.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Preserve required origin attribution, meaningful transformation history, significant execution checkpoints, tamper-evident audit evidence and end-to-end traceability. Harmonia SHALL preserve provenance, audit and operational evidence where required by governing obligations, architectural significance, accountability, reconstruction, security or assurance needs. Routine technical activity SHALL NOT automatically require durable evidentiary recording.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Recording attributable, verifiable origin metadata for information sources, authors, and timestamps.



\item
Tracking information-significant transformation history and required mapping checkpoints as information crosses system seams.



\item
Capturing non-PHI operational and security audit trails for regulatory compliance (HIPAA, GDPR).



\item
Supporting end-to-end transaction tracing across asynchronous processing pipelines.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Participating elements preserve required provenance and audit context according to policy. Telemetry, operational facts, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct. Being evidence is contextual, not an intrinsic property of every recorded fact; preservation does not establish an assurance conclusion.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Telemetry, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct. Recording evidence neither establishes an assurance conclusion nor automatically requires retention of routine technical activity.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Trust, Accountability \& Assurance; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Operational Assurance preserves processing integrity under concurrency, duplicate delivery and failure. It brings together resilience, durable ingress acceptance, recovery and operational telemetry so that technical degradation does not silently weaken the managed operation's semantics. Its contribution is collaborative across operational boundaries while remaining a bounded architectural responsibility.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Ensure concurrency integrity, system resilience, duplicate detection, exception handling, automated recovery, and operational telemetry across platform operations.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Enforcing sliding-window duplicate message detection and idempotent suppression.



\item
Guaranteeing ingress dual-write safety (durable acceptance before emitting positive application ACK).



\item
Managing structured failure recovery, exception escalation, and dead-letter isolation.



\item
Emitting platform telemetry, operational health metrics, and queue processing metrics.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Realized collaboratively across boundary gateways, messaging infrastructure, execution workers, and storage layers.



\end{itemize}
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{EC-12 /\allowbreak{} EC-14 Boundary}

EC-12 retains the established scope and responsibilities above. It may contribute directly to generic operational/\allowbreak{}processing assurance, limited to that contribution in the \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md\#collaborative-enterprise-capability-contribution-matrix}{approved assurance matrix}. It does not own the general semantics of assurance disposition, assurance-specific criteria applicability, evidentiary association, assessment against assurance criteria, adjudication, or independent assurance findings and conclusions. Those distinguishing responsibilities are introduced through EC-14 Service Guardian. Operational health and business-level processing assurance remain distinct; EC-12 is not expanded to absorb EC-14.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Operational health is distinct from independent assessment of a governed subject. Assurance-specific criteria applicability, adjudication and conclusions belong to the established EC-14 contribution.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Trust, Accountability \& Assurance; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Service Guardian supplies the reusable assurance semantics that bind a governed subject to applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence, support assessment and adjudication, and establish reportable findings. Its contribution distinguishes explicit evidence insufficiency from a conclusion about the subject. Existing Enterprise Capabilities contribute collaboratively; EC-14 does not duplicate all their information, policy or execution responsibilities.


Independence concerns control of evaluation and conclusion. A subject may supply evidence but cannot solely determine, suppress or retrospectively change its own assurance outcome.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Service Guardian provides the reusable capability to independently establish whether governed service behaviour, state or outcomes remain within defined assurance expectations by associating applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence with a governed subject, assessing that evidence, adjudicating the assessment, and establishing reportable assurance findings and conclusions.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Supplying assurance-specific semantics for assurance disposition and assurance criteria applicability.



\item
Associating a governed subject/\allowbreak{}context with applicable criteria and sufficient trustworthy evidence for a particular assurance purpose.



\item
Assessing evidence against applicable criteria and adjudicating assessed detail to establish reportable findings, exceptions and conclusions.



\item
Preserving assurance independence, temporal/\allowbreak{}version-specific evidence and criteria applicability, and explicit inability to establish a conclusion where evidence is insufficient.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Supplies the assurance-specific semantics required to bind existing reusable capabilities into governed assurance. It contributes directly to Assurance Design, Assurance Criteria Management and Governed Assurance; direct contribution is not sole realisation. The \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md\#collaborative-enterprise-capability-contribution-matrix}{approved matrix} preserves the contributions of EC-01 through EC-13.



\item
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not own the underlying governed subject, authoritative governance requirements, or source information used as evidence. Does not perform, manage, remediate, assign, delegate or operationally escalate the subject activity. Does not replace System Operations or EC-12 Operational Assurance, and does not provide Clinical Services Delivery Assurance.



\item
\textbf{Allocation Boundary}: No strategic logical component, application component, runtime service or implementation construct is allocated EC-14. The catalogue defines a capability, not a software component or deployment boundary.



\end{itemize}
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Conceptual Behavioural Sequence}

\textit{RAD source listing (presentation only; no inferred ancestry).}
\begin{quote}
Define Good Behaviour

↓

Gather Evidence

↓

Assess Evidence against Good Behaviour

↓

Adjudicate Assessed Detail

↓

Report
\end{quote}

This sequence explains the capability; it is not an implementation workflow specification or a derived Business Process. “Define Good Behaviour” identifies assurance expectations and criteria; it does not transfer ownership of governing requirements to Service Guardian. Source information ownership remains with its responsible capability; assurance owns its contextual evidentiary association.


The \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#health-service-assurance-approved-business-enabling-capabilities}{Business Enabling assurance principles} govern disposition, generic processing assurance, evidence/\allowbreak{}criteria temporality, assessment/\allowbreak{}adjudication, independence, failure/\allowbreak{}recovery and explicit evidence insufficiency. These semantics are not universally reducible to PASS /\allowbreak{} FAIL /\allowbreak{} UNKNOWN and do not imply an assurance information model or persistence mechanism.


\par\smallskip

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

The capability does not manage or remediate the subject, replace operational assurance, or assure clinical adequacy. No application component, runtime service or deployment boundary is allocated, and the explanatory sequence is not a derived Business Process.

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Trust, Accountability \& Assurance; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Managed State \& Lifecycle provides reusable responsibility for valid progression, temporal applicability and non-destructive change. A directory relationship, clinical document and operational work item have different business states, yet all need an intelligible distinction between current standing, historical state and invalid transitions. The capability captures that recurrence without replacing each subject's lifecycle meaning.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Govern the current and historical state, effective temporal periods, state transition validations, and lifecycle progression of managed integration artifacts and entities.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Defining and enforcing valid state transition state machines (e.g., \texttt{\seqsplit{REQUESTED}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{VALIDATED}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{IN\_PROGRESS}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{COMPLETED}}).



\item
Maintaining temporal validity intervals (effective start and end dates) for relationships, credentials, and states.



\item
Supporting non-destructive state progression, preserving historical state versions for longitudinal review.



\item
Rejecting illegal or out-of-order state transitions while accommodating idempotent replay.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not define thread-level mutexes or database transaction isolation levels.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Business lifecycle integrity does not prescribe locks, database isolation or worker implementation, and illustrative state names do not define every subject's transitions.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Governed Information Operations; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Information Management provides the recurring ability to represent and maintain governed information through validation, preservation, retrieval and versioned change. It accommodates both responsive active use and authoritative durable preservation while keeping those responsibilities separate. This distinction allows availability and working state to support care without turning a cache into durable truth.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Validate, represent, persist, retrieve, version, and manage governed clinical, administrative, and operational information assets.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Validating inbound information structures against canonical information constraints.



\item
Providing authoritative durable persistence for historical health records and administrative registries.



\item
Managing active distributed working memory representations for low-latency retrieval.



\item
Governing document versioning, supersession, amendments, and retractions without data loss.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Architectural Principle}: Enforces the foundational separation between \emph{active distributed state access} and \emph{authoritative durable state preservation} (Axiom AX-05).



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Engine capabilities provide machinery under Harmonia semantics. Persistence success does not establish information authority or make the platform the originator of the represented facts.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Governed Information Operations; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Search \& Discovery makes information, entities and service endpoints findable through governed criteria and bounded queries. It addresses the recurring need to locate relevant material or a destination before it can be used. Security-qualified results preserve the distinction between knowing that something exists and being entitled to obtain or disclose it.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Index, search, resolve, filter, and discover information assets, entities, directory endpoints, and healthcare services across the enterprise.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Providing multi-criteria indexed search across complex entity graphs (e.g., find active cardiologists at Location X accepting new referrals).



\item
Resolving service and practitioner communication endpoints for addressed delivery.



\item
Supporting bounded, paginated clinical queries across longitudinal patient records.



\item
Applying dynamic security and consent filters to search results prior to egress.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not dictate specific search engine indexes, inverted index implementations, or SQL query syntaxes.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Discovery does not decide policy or prescribe a search engine, index format or query language.

Interoperability \& Exchange moves information across participating boundaries through destination resolution, transformation, delivery and acknowledgements. It preserves the difference between technical transmission and the recipient's business response so that an exchange can be understood under its actual contract. Standards govern the external representation while internal management semantics remain private.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Resolve destinations, transform schemas, route, transport, deliver, acknowledge, and coordinate standards-based information exchange across enterprise boundaries.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Providing multi-protocol boundary adaptation for healthcare standards (HL7 v2, FHIR REST, DICOM, secure messaging).



\item
Executing bidirectional structural and semantic transformations between legacy formats and canonical representations.



\item
Ensuring reliable addressed delivery and fan-out distribution to external clinical endpoints.



\item
Processing and distinguishing technical delivery acknowledgements from business acknowledgements.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Boundary Rule}: Egress terminates Harmonia management of the emitted representation (Axiom AX-13).



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Egress ends Harmonia management of the emitted representation. Retained delivery evidence does not extend control over an external recipient or transfer payload authority.

Event \& Subscription connects significant changes with participants whose registered interests match them. The architectural meaning is the relationship between a change and an interested consumer, rather than the broker constructs used to carry it.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Publish, ingest, correlate, filter, and syndicate events and subscription-driven changes across the enterprise landscape.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

Ingesting operational and clinical event triggers from external systems and internal state changes.

\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Instantiating operational work items (Work Orders, To Dos, synthetic platform Tasks) in response to triggers.



\item
Matching and assigning work units to eligible human or automated performers and roles based on policy rules.



\item
Dispatching work units to their assigned performers with acknowledgement according to the applicable interaction contract.



\item
Supervising execution progress, tracking timeouts, managing escalations, and handling activity interruptions.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Decoupling Note}: Free of worker threads, thread pools, execution daemons, or specific workflow runtime engines.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Coordination does not confer clinical work allocation or judgement. The capability specifies neither worker threads nor a particular execution engine.

Policy \& Control supplies the reusable evaluation and enforcement of authority, consent, privacy and handling constraints. Its purpose is consistent governed action across ingress, information access, execution and presentation boundaries. Default-deny evaluation preserves the need for established authority rather than treating a caller's intent or a technically valid request as permission.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Evaluate and enforce security, consent, privacy, and regulatory policies including authority, access control, and information handling rules.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Executing impartial, default-deny policy evaluations for all integration transactions.



\item
Enforcing Role-Based and Attribute-Based Access Control (RBAC/\allowbreak{}ABAC) policies.



\item
Evaluating patient consent directives and privacy restrictions at boundary and query checkpoints.



\item
Enforcing statutory information disclosure boundaries (e.g., mental health, VIP records).



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Evaluated across boundary gateways, internal bus dispatch, storage interfaces, and presentation layers.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Participation at multiple enforcement points does not distribute policy ownership or turn operational security context into persistent clinical content.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Provenance \& Traceability preserves the meaningful attribution and history needed to explain information and significant activity. It connects source, transformation and required checkpoints without making every internal mechanism permanent evidence. Its recurring contribution supports accountability, reconstruction and assurance use while retaining the context that makes a recorded fact evidentially relevant.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Preserve required origin attribution, meaningful transformation history, significant execution checkpoints, tamper-evident audit evidence and end-to-end traceability. Harmonia SHALL preserve provenance, audit and operational evidence where required by governing obligations, architectural significance, accountability, reconstruction, security or assurance needs. Routine technical activity SHALL NOT automatically require durable evidentiary recording.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Recording attributable, verifiable origin metadata for information sources, authors, and timestamps.



\item
Tracking information-significant transformation history and required mapping checkpoints as information crosses system seams.



\item
Capturing non-PHI operational and security audit trails for regulatory compliance (HIPAA, GDPR).



\item
Supporting end-to-end transaction tracing across asynchronous processing pipelines.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Participating elements preserve required provenance and audit context according to policy. Telemetry, operational facts, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct. Being evidence is contextual, not an intrinsic property of every recorded fact; preservation does not establish an assurance conclusion.



\end{itemize}

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Telemetry, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct. Recording evidence neither establishes an assurance conclusion nor automatically requires retention of routine technical activity.

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Trust, Accountability \& Assurance; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Operational Assurance preserves processing integrity under concurrency, duplicate delivery and failure. It brings together resilience, durable ingress acceptance, recovery and operational telemetry so that technical degradation does not silently weaken the managed operation's semantics. Its contribution is collaborative across operational boundaries while remaining a bounded architectural responsibility.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Ensure concurrency integrity, system resilience, duplicate detection, exception handling, automated recovery, and operational telemetry across platform operations.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Enforcing sliding-window duplicate message detection and idempotent suppression.



\item
Guaranteeing ingress dual-write safety (durable acceptance before emitting positive application ACK).



\item
Managing structured failure recovery, exception escalation, and dead-letter isolation.



\item
Emitting platform telemetry, operational health metrics, and queue processing metrics.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Realized collaboratively across boundary gateways, messaging infrastructure, execution workers, and storage layers.



\end{itemize}
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{EC-12 /\allowbreak{} EC-14 Boundary}

EC-12 retains the established scope and responsibilities above. It may contribute directly to generic operational/\allowbreak{}processing assurance, limited to that contribution in the \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md\#collaborative-enterprise-capability-contribution-matrix}{approved assurance matrix}. It does not own the general semantics of assurance disposition, assurance-specific criteria applicability, evidentiary association, assessment against assurance criteria, adjudication, or independent assurance findings and conclusions. Those distinguishing responsibilities are introduced through EC-14 Service Guardian. Operational health and business-level processing assurance remain distinct; EC-12 is not expanded to absorb EC-14.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Operational health is distinct from independent assessment of a governed subject. Assurance-specific criteria applicability, adjudication and conclusions belong to the established EC-14 contribution.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Proposed Placement Rationale}

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Trust, Accountability \& Assurance; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Service Guardian supplies the reusable assurance semantics that bind a governed subject to applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence, support assessment and adjudication, and establish reportable findings. Its contribution distinguishes explicit evidence insufficiency from a conclusion about the subject. Existing Enterprise Capabilities contribute collaboratively; EC-14 does not duplicate all their information, policy or execution responsibilities.


Independence concerns control of evaluation and conclusion. A subject may supply evidence but cannot solely determine, suppress or retrospectively change its own assurance outcome.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

\begin{itemize}

\item
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Service Guardian provides the reusable capability to independently establish whether governed service behaviour, state or outcomes remain within defined assurance expectations by associating applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence with a governed subject, assessing that evidence, adjudicating the assessment, and establishing reportable assurance findings and conclusions.



\item
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item
Supplying assurance-specific semantics for assurance disposition and assurance criteria applicability.



\item
Associating a governed subject/\allowbreak{}context with applicable criteria and sufficient trustworthy evidence for a particular assurance purpose.



\item
Assessing evidence against applicable criteria and adjudicating assessed detail to establish reportable findings, exceptions and conclusions.



\item
Preserving assurance independence, temporal/\allowbreak{}version-specific evidence and criteria applicability, and explicit inability to establish a conclusion where evidence is insufficient.



\end{itemize}


\item
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Supplies the assurance-specific semantics required to bind existing reusable capabilities into governed assurance. It contributes directly to Assurance Design, Assurance Criteria Management and Governed Assurance; direct contribution is not sole realisation. The \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md\#collaborative-enterprise-capability-contribution-matrix}{approved matrix} preserves the contributions of EC-01 through EC-13.



\item
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not own the underlying governed subject, authoritative governance requirements, or source information used as evidence. Does not perform, manage, remediate, assign, delegate or operationally escalate the subject activity. Does not replace System Operations or EC-12 Operational Assurance, and does not provide Clinical Services Delivery Assurance.



\item
\textbf{Allocation Boundary}: No strategic logical component, application component, runtime service or implementation construct is allocated EC-14. The catalogue defines a capability, not a software component or deployment boundary.



\end{itemize}
\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Conceptual Behavioural Sequence}

\textit{RAD source listing (presentation only; no inferred ancestry).}
\begin{quote}
Define Good Behaviour

↓

Gather Evidence

↓

Assess Evidence against Good Behaviour

↓

Adjudicate Assessed Detail

↓

Report
\end{quote}

This sequence explains the capability; it is not an implementation workflow specification or a derived Business Process. “Define Good Behaviour” identifies assurance expectations and criteria; it does not transfer ownership of governing requirements to Service Guardian. Source information ownership remains with its responsible capability; assurance owns its contextual evidentiary association.


The \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#health-service-assurance-approved-business-enabling-capabilities}{Business Enabling assurance principles} govern disposition, generic processing assurance, evidence/\allowbreak{}criteria temporality, assessment/\allowbreak{}adjudication, independence, failure/\allowbreak{}recovery and explicit evidence insufficiency. These semantics are not universally reducible to PASS /\allowbreak{} FAIL /\allowbreak{} UNKNOWN and do not imply an assurance information model or persistence mechanism.


\par\smallskip

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

The capability does not manage or remediate the subject, replace operational assurance, or assure clinical adequacy. No application component, runtime service or deployment boundary is allocated, and the explanatory sequence is not a derived Business Process.

The established reusable responsibility is a constituent ability of Trust, Accountability \& Assurance; its canonical scope and exclusions remain unchanged.

\cataloguefield{section}{Capability Overview}

Individual Care Delivery is the organisation's ability to understand an individual's health and act on that understanding through purposeful care. Its six constituent abilities distinguish establishing findings, interpreting their clinical meaning, choosing a response, performing care, observing change and evaluating care against its objectives. These distinctions describe responsibilities and outcomes rather than a compulsory sequence: a consultation or continuing episode may revisit several of them.


The same ability can be exercised in a hospital, a general practice, a home or a virtual consultation. Setting and time pattern affect the circumstances of care without changing the responsibility represented by this capability.


\cataloguefield{section}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Assess, clinically determine, plan, intervene, monitor and review individual care independently of setting, mode, time pattern or organisational arrangement.


\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}

Support clinically meaningful care whose intent, performance, observed effects and continuing appropriateness can be distinguished.


\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Care access, appointments and operational coordination enable care but do not establish that it has been performed. Clinical judgement and the authority to deliver care remain with the responsible participants; possession or coordination of their information does not transfer that authority to Harmonia.


\cataloguefield{section}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Harmonia supplies and connects information used in individual care. The approved Health Information Access support trace is bounded: records can inform care, but direct assessment can establish findings independently, and access to a proposed intervention does not authorise its performance.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Assessment establishes what is currently known about an individual's health through history, examination and measurement. Within Individual Care Delivery it supplies assessed findings, including findings obtained directly from the person rather than retrieved from an existing record. Its three children distinguish ways of establishing knowledge, rather than professions, clinical specialties or locations.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

The capability to establish an understanding of an individual's current health state through the collection, consideration and evaluation of relevant clinical, health and contextual information.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Give subsequent clinical interpretation a defensible account of the person's current state and relevant history.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Finding an abnormal measurement is distinguishable from deciding what it means clinically. Diagnosis, prognosis, selection of care and performance of care belong to adjacent abilities.

Health History Assessment establishes clinically relevant understanding from a person's history and its surrounding context. Within assessment it contributes knowledge that a current examination or measurement alone may not reveal, while requiring consideration of the relevance of historical information to the present situation. Access to previous records can assist, but the responsibility is the assessment of history rather than retrieval itself.

Establish relevant health knowledge from the individual’s history and applicable historical/\allowbreak{}contextual information.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Clinical Examination establishes findings through examination of the individual. \cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

It marks the transition from intended care to care actually performed, whether the action seeks to alter, maintain or otherwise manage health. Its exercise can establish that treatment occurred even when the desired clinical result was not achieved.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

The capability to perform clinical actions intended to alter, maintain or otherwise manage an individual's health state in accordance with an established care intent.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Put the intended clinical response into practice through appropriately authorised care.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Orders and appointments express or arrange future activity; they are not evidence that the intervention occurred. Therapy, medication and procedural examples do not constitute an approved three-child taxonomy: that proposed decomposition remains provisional.

Health State Monitoring establishes the aggregate temporally situated view; Care Response Monitoring considers that view in relation to a particular condition and treatment. Together they distinguish observation over time from a single measurement and from the clinical judgement prompted by a trend.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

The capability to observe and evaluate an individual's health state over time in order to identify clinically meaningful change, stability or deviation from an expected state or trajectory.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Make relevant trajectories visible while preserving what was observed and what still requires interpretation.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Monitoring does not establish the clinical significance of a change or judge whether care achieved its objectives. Those responsibilities remain Clinical Determination and Individual Care Review respectively.

Establish an aggregate, temporally situated view of the individual’s health from applicable monitored data.

Establish whether continuing the current approach is justified and whether reconsideration is needed.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Evaluate whether the current intended care remains suitable in the individual’s current context.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Care Access Management establishes the circumstances in which an individual seeks or enters care. Intake creates the access context, referral requests another participant's involvement, and eligibility determines whether applicable access conditions are met. These are separate contributions to access: a person can be eligible without having a booking, and a received referral can remain undecided.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Establish and manage access to applicable care.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Make entry requirements and referral disposition intelligible without implying that care has already been accepted or delivered.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Eligibility does not allocate care, and referral receipt does not establish an assumption of clinical responsibility.

Support care requirements with an operationally credible combination of time, place, resources and capacity.

Its contribution is the operational application of resources, without changing the authoritative facts that make their use legitimate.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Apply legitimately available and appropriately authorised resources to a current or planned operational care requirement, particularly using roster/\allowbreak{}on-call and service-coverage context.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

Deployment is neither roster authoring nor clinical work assignment and does not confer clinical authority or ownership of enterprise assets.

\cataloguefield{section}{Capability Overview}

This capability addresses operational clinical quality and safety, including concerns, incidents, response and improvement. Its established safety branch distinguishes risk identification, prospective mitigation and active response. Its quality branch distinguishes criteria, evidence, assessment and reporting. Together these make it possible to reason about clinical quality without equating an observation, a judgement and the action taken in response.


\cataloguefield{section}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Operational clinical quality, safety and improvement: monitoring clinical outcomes; identifying quality and safety concerns; adverse event and incident management, reporting and response; infection control; operational quality and safety monitoring; continuous quality improvement; and coordination of operational responses to identified concerns.


\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}

Support recognition and management of clinical safety concerns and informed improvement of clinical quality.


\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary}

This is neither a generic enterprise incident container nor a replacement for macro-level Health Service Assurance. Its bounded decomposition does not exhaust clinical quality and safety practice.


\cataloguefield{section}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Information about outcomes, risks, incidents and operational responses materially supports these responsibilities. Integrating that evidence does not assign clinical quality judgement or originating clinical authority to the platform.

Its four children preserve the difference between the expected standard, the material considered, the assessment reached and the report of that assessment. This supports scrutiny of why a quality conclusion is justified rather than treating the presence of measurements as a judgement.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Manage the clinical-quality distinctions materially required for R1/\allowbreak{}R2.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Make clinical-quality conclusions understandable in relation to their criteria, evidence and assessment authority.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Reporting does not originate the conclusion or perform subsequent improvement. Neither a separate monitoring provider nor generic Continuous Improvement placement is established by this decomposition.

Understand population-health state and manage organised surveillance, significant events and applicable notification.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Make population-health concerns and applicable communication obligations visible in their population and temporal context.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Notification management does not define the obligation or own the operational response. Surveillance evidence can inform other abilities without establishing their findings.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Health-System Planning considers the capacity and service footprint required to meet assessed demand. Demand Assessment establishes the basis and scale of need, Capacity Planning determines what is required, and Distribution Planning addresses where that capacity should sit across the service network. The decomposition preserves the difference between understanding demand and deciding a response to it.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Assess health-service demand and plan the capacity and footprint required to meet it.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Support a defensible relationship between expected demand and the planned scale and distribution of health services.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Plans do not establish available resources or operational allocations. Detailed commissioning, capital, funding and workforce planning remain deliberately unmodelled.

Identify, extract, formulate, associate, govern and share reusable clinical knowledge.

Make reusable clinical knowledge available with the qualifications and approval standing needed to judge its use.

Publication does not establish applicability to an individual or a clinical decision. Concept association does not redefine terminology, and formulation does not constitute approval.

Identity Assurance establishes confidence that a person is who they claim to be using appropriate evidence and processes. It concerns the basis and strength of the identity claim, rather than only successful use of an authentication mechanism. Within identity governance it makes confidence a question that can be considered separately from contextual sufficiency and access authority.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Establish sufficient confidence that a person is who they claim to be through appropriate evidence and processes.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}

An assured identity is not automatically sufficient for every context or permitted to perform every action.

\cataloguefield{section}{Capability Overview}

Health Service Governance establishes the normative envelope within which health-service activity operates: what obligations apply, who may decide, what constraints bind decisions and how adherence will be assessed and reported. Its framework and compliance branches distinguish the authoritative requirements from the arrangements used to judge satisfaction. Governance therefore shapes legitimate activity without becoming the manager of every governed operation.


\cataloguefield{section}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Establish and maintain the obligations, authorities, constraints, policies and governance framework under which health-service activity must operate, and define how adherence will be assessed, checked and reported.


\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}

Make obligations, decision authority and compliance expectations explicit and traceable.


\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary}

Operational management chooses and progresses means within the governing envelope; assurance evaluates evidence. Neither responsibility is absorbed merely because governance defines its constraints.


\cataloguefield{section}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance — v0.1 explanation}

Formal relevance remains Unresolved. The requirements plainly constrain managed activity, but the RAD has not assigned enough platform participation or enabling derivation to adjudicate its relevance classification.


\cataloguefield{section}{Preserved v0.1 Review Matters}

No Business Enabling derivation is established for Health Service Governance.

\cataloguefield{section}{Capability Overview}

Health Service Assurance establishes justified confidence in the ability to deliver health services appropriately. Specification defines how confidence will be established; evaluation determines what the available evidence supports. Its subject is macro-level service delivery, with workforce, clinical, information, security and other concerns contributing evidence or criteria without becoming separate assurance trees.


Where independent governed assurance is required, the subject cannot control its own evaluation or conclusion. Independence concerns control of the assurance judgement rather than requiring a separate organisation or technology installation.


\cataloguefield{section}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Establish and maintain justified confidence that health services can be, and are being, delivered in accordance with applicable expectations, obligations, constraints and required levels of performance.


\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}

Distinguish justified confidence, qualified conclusions and insufficient evidence so that assurance communicates what is actually supported.


\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary}

Assurance manages its own evaluation and does not assign, remediate or progress the subject activity. Harmonia does not thereby assume responsibility for clinical adequacy or professional practice.


\cataloguefield{section}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Approved independent governed assurance materially supports service confidence. The three established assurance BECs provide bounded support; they are not remapped to the newer BC descendants and are not assigned implementation components.

\cataloguefield{section}{Capability Overview}

Individual Care Delivery is the organisation's ability to understand an individual's health and act on that understanding through purposeful care. Its six constituent abilities distinguish establishing findings, interpreting their clinical meaning, choosing a response, performing care, observing change and evaluating care against its objectives. These distinctions describe responsibilities and outcomes rather than a compulsory sequence: a consultation or continuing episode may revisit several of them.


The same ability can be exercised in a hospital, a general practice, a home or a virtual consultation. Setting and time pattern affect the circumstances of care without changing the responsibility represented by this capability.


\cataloguefield{section}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

Assess, clinically determine, plan, intervene, monitor and review individual care independently of setting, mode, time pattern or organisational arrangement.


\cataloguefield{section}{Intent}

Support clinically meaningful care whose intent, performance, observed effects and continuing appropriateness can be distinguished.


\cataloguefield{section}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Care access, appointments and operational coordination enable care but do not establish that it has been performed. Clinical judgement and the authority to deliver care remain with the responsible participants; possession or coordination of their information does not transfer that authority to Harmonia.


\cataloguefield{section}{Harmonia Architectural Relevance}

Harmonia supplies and connects information used in individual care. The approved Health Information Access support trace is bounded: records can inform care, but direct assessment can establish findings independently, and access to a proposed intervention does not authorise its performance.

Assessment establishes what is currently known about an individual's health through history, examination and measurement. Within Individual Care Delivery it supplies assessed findings, including findings obtained directly from the person rather than retrieved from an existing record. Its three children distinguish ways of establishing knowledge, rather than professions, clinical specialties or locations.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

The capability to establish an understanding of an individual's current health state through the collection, consideration and evaluation of relevant clinical, health and contextual information.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Give subsequent clinical interpretation a defensible account of the person's current state and relevant history.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Finding an abnormal measurement is distinguishable from deciding what it means clinically. Diagnosis, prognosis, selection of care and performance of care belong to adjacent abilities.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Clinical Intervention is the ability to perform a clinical action under an established care intent. It marks the transition from intended care to care actually performed, whether the action seeks to alter, maintain or otherwise manage health. Its exercise can establish that treatment occurred even when the desired clinical result was not achieved.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

The capability to perform clinical actions intended to alter, maintain or otherwise manage an individual's health state in accordance with an established care intent.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Put the intended clinical response into practice through appropriately authorised care.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary}

Orders and appointments express or arrange future activity; they are not evidence that the intervention occurred. Therapy, medication and procedural examples do not constitute an approved three-child taxonomy: that proposed decomposition remains provisional.

DN-BC-010 retains the intervention candidate as provisional pending a coherent peer taxonomy.

\cataloguefield{subsection}{Capability Overview}

Monitoring develops a view of an individual's health over time so that change, stability or deviation can be recognised. Health State Monitoring establishes the aggregate temporally situated view; Care Response Monitoring considers that view in relation to a particular condition and treatment. Together they distinguish observation over time from a single measurement and from the clinical judgement prompted by a trend.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Definition / governed semantic detail}

The capability to observe and evaluate an individual's health state over time in order to identify clinically meaningful change, stability or deviation from an expected state or trajectory.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Intent}

Make relevant trajectories visible while preserving what was observed and what still requires interpretation.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Monitoring does not establish the clinical significance of a change or judge whether care achieved its objectives. Those responsibilities remain Clinical Determination and Individual Care Review respectively.

Establish whether continuing the current approach is justified and whether reconsideration is needed.


\cataloguefield{subsection}{Boundary — v0.1 explanation}

Evaluate whether the current intended care remains suitable in the individual’s current context.


\cataloguefield{subsubsection}{Boundary}
